text:
Marco Rossi came to Vancouver in the Quinn Hughes trade, and against Minnesota he finally played the game that trade was supposed to produce: 19:30 of ice, 12 of 16 faceoffs, two goals including the late tying one, and a shootout win. Daniel Wagner called it "a beastly game by Marco Rossi against his former team."

The rest of his season has been thinner: nine points in 24 games at 15:26 a night, and a point rate (1.46 per 60) well below his talent range. That gap usually closes. His finishing is honest, five goals on 4.0 expected, and Vancouver has scored 3.6 fewer goals than expected with him on. The Canucks lose the chance battle with him on (42% of the five-on-five expected goals), but they're 3.5 points better than without him, which tells you more about the team. He exits the zone with possession 70% of the time in Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking. Our range projects 30 to 48 points. Nights like that one are the argument for more minutes.
